SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: Participants included 117 undergraduate students (66 male and 51 female, M age = 20.1, SD = 1.6 years) enrolled in a Theories of Personality psychology course at Harvard College. A total of 53 students (32 males and 21 females) retook the test.

Effects.evidence_source: No correlation coefficients between intelligence and creative achievement were reported in the text.

Creativity Measures.evidence_source: A computerized version of the CAQ was administered to students in a computer lab.

Domain classified.evidence_source: A computerized version of the CAQ was administered to students in a computer lab. The CAQ measures creative achievement in various domains, and no specific domain was highlighted, thus 'Total' is inferred.

Number of studies.evidence_source: The text describes a single study involving participants from Harvard College, with data collected at two time points (Time 1 and Time 2) for the same group of students or a subset thereof.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the methodology of a study involving 117 undergraduate students from Harvard College (mean age = 20.1 years). Participants completed a computerized version of the Creativity Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ) at Time 1. A subset of 53 students later retook the CAQ at Time 2, with an average of 51 days between administrations.
